newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian call money inactive, gilt prices harden.
newsitem.headline: Indian call money inactive, gilt prices harden.

text.p: Indian call money ended Friday unchanged in the 0.10-0.25 percent range with no trades reported, dealers said.
Banks do not normally borrow on reporting days as this increases their reserve requirements for the next fortnight.

Dealers said three-day money was quoted in the 1.25-1.50 percent range towards close of trade. Rates opened the day in the 2.0-2.25 percent range but came down on lack of demand and good supply, they said.
Dealers said prices of government securities continued to firm up in active trade.
"Demand for securities remains good as call money is low," said a dealer at a state-run bank. "This has been pushing prices by a few basis points every day for the past couple of weeks."
Dealers said buying interest which had been largely concentrated in short-dated securities in the past few days spread to medium-term stocks also on Friday.
They said the Reserve Bank of India put some medium-term securities on its sale list on Friday and this affected the market sentiment.
Traded volumes on the National Stock Exchange were around 5.40 billion rupees against Thursday's 6.05 billion, a trader at a securities firm said.
The 13.50 percent 1998 government of India stock firmed up to 103.30 rupees from its last traded price of 103.20 while the 13.70 percent 1999 rose to 102.70 from 102.57, dealers said.
Treasury bills maturing in April 1997 were traded on Friday at a yield of 7.40 percent against 7.55.
Dealers said there were no trades in commercial paper or certificates of deposit.
